open_issues.text: deferred minor finding packages/orch/scripts/ro-run.py:53: The RO_RUN_RW_ESCAPE check only looks at --rw paths inside DIR. `ro-run.py --protect /w --rw /w -- cmd` passes, because the path is inside-or-equal and not a symlink. `--protect /w --rw /home/u` (an ancestor) passes unchecked. Either way the whole protected tree becomes writable with exit 0, although --protect is meant to be fail-closed (D11). The shipped catalog entries cannot reach this. The runtime --rw addition in roles.py:381 only targets the executor, which has no --protect. A future caller or hand-written argv can.

open_issues.text: deferred minor finding packages/orch/scripts/ro-run.py:47: The overlap check only tests whether DIR is inside a default writable root. It does not test whether a default root resolves inside DIR. With HOME inside the checkout (or ~/.grok a symlink into it), `<checkout>/.grok` stays writable under --protect. A protected role can then write files into the checkout, including Grok's own config directory.

open_issues.text: deferred minor finding packages/orch/tests/test_ro_run.py:112: ProtectedRunTests.setUp creates its checkout in `SCRIPT.parents[3]`, assumed to be the repo root. If the repo sits under /tmp, /var/tmp or ~/.grok, the probe exits 3 with RO_RUN_PROTECT_OVERLAP. setUp only skips on LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE and ABI_TOO_OLD, so the next assertEqual fails instead of skipping. In an own-repo layout (module split) parents[3] is no longer the repo root. A killed run also leaves `.ro-run-test-*` in the repo root. The guidance suggested a directory under ~/.cache.

open_issues.text: deferred nit finding packages/orch/scripts/ro-run.py:104: On a kernel without Landlock, the syscall returns -1. With --protect the user sees `LANDLOCK_ABI_TOO_OLD: -1` and never gets LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE with the errno text. The same Landlock-less kernel without --protect still reports LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE. The contract says ABI < 3, so this is defensible. The message is misleading.
